title: European Commission reports progress on global biodiversity restoration targets
excerpt: Commissioner Roswall stated that restoration efforts are underway but remain behind the pace required to meet 2030 goals.
bodyHtml:
On October 28, 2026, the European Commission reported that restoration of ecosystems is occurring globally, though not at the scale needed to meet Target 2 of the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework. This target calls for the effective restoration of at least 30% of degraded terrestrial, inland water, coastal, and marine ecosystems by 2030.

Commissioner Roswall noted that the European Union's Nature Restoration Regulation aims to deliver restoration measures on at least 20% of land and sea by 2030. The Commission stated that governments are beginning to commit resources to these efforts, citing a fund of nearly 6 billion euro in Denmark to support changes in land use and peatland restoration.

The European Commission also noted that nature-negative finance reached around 6.5 trillion euro in 2023. According to the Commission, achieving the goals of the Global Biodiversity Framework requires aligning financial flows with nature-positive development and ensuring that nature has a seat in corporate boardrooms.
topic: Commissioner Roswall's address at a High-level side-event at CBD COP17, “Restoring nature – from commitments to action”
